key_insight: OmniShotCut reframes shot-boundary detection as a structured relational prediction task: a Shot-Query Transformer jointly models shots and their pairwise relations to produce more interpretable, holistic boundary decisions and catch subtle discontinuities.
problem_solved: Addresses noisy, low-diversity annotations and non-interpretable/missed boundaries from current SBD methods by modeling global context and explicit shot relations rather than independent local frame decisions.
method: Shot-Query Transformer — use learned shot queries that attend to video features and to each other to represent shots and transitions holistically.
Joint relational prediction — predict shot boundaries and inter-shot relation labels (e.g., abrupt, gradual, transitional) via cross-query interactions and relational loss terms.
Improved data & evaluation — train/evaluate with higher-diversity annotations and updated benchmarks to reduce annotation noise and better reflect real-world transitions.
impact: Provides more reliable, interpretable shot segmentation for video indexing, editing, and downstream vision tasks, reducing missed subtle discontinuities and improving benchmark fidelity for future SBD research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → backbone features → shot queries → transformer cross-attention → predicted boundaries and relations.
Attention map visualization: query-to-frame and query-to-query attention highlighting how the model reasons across time and between shots.
Before/after examples: sample transitions showing prior methods’ false/missed boundaries vs. OmniShotCut’s corrected, labeled boundaries.
Benchmark chart: precision/recall or error-rate comparison on old vs. new annotated datasets to show robustness gains (no raw numbers required).
paper_title: OmniShotCut: Holistic Relational Shot Boundary Detection with Shot-Query Transformer
paper_authors: Boyang Wang, Guangyi Xu, Zhipeng Tang, Jiahui Zhang, Zezhou Cheng
